To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the observed M_BH vs sigma relation can be understood as a consequence of the collapse of gas in a dark halo potential, if the collapse is regulated or suppressed by the radiation from a central black hole.

we can explain the formation of elliptical galaxies and the M-sigma relation by the collapse of gas in the cusp region of dark matter halos, and that we can explain why ellipticals are so red by the radiation of their central black holes.
the formation of bulges in dark halos is as fast as the formation of central black holes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of spheroidal stellar galaxies, and the formation of supermassive black holes (BHs) in their nuclei.
the formation of bulges/ellipsoids as fast as central BHs in dark galaxy halos.
the formation of bulges/ellipsoids in dark halos and with their central supermassive black holes (SMBH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the observed bulge/elliptical galaxies and central black holes are formed together and simultaneously, in a very short time, by a single process.
the formation of bulges and elliptical galaxies as well as the formation of supermassive black holes are two sides of the same coin.
the formation of the central bulge and the central BH in a galaxy halo can occur in a single process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of bulges/ellipitcals and black holes in galaxies are tightly connected and can be explained by a single physical process.
we have shown how to form bulges and central black holes in galaxy halos as fast and in as many as the starburst galaxies.
we can explain the origin of both the bulge and BH in one model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the observed M_BH vs v_sigma relation is a natural consequence of the formation process, and does not need any special initial conditions, such as a gas free initial state.
the formation time of a spheroidal system is of the order of the collapse time of a gas sphere.
bulges and ellipticals are not necessarily formed in the central regions, but can be formed in the outer parts of dark halos.
